title: Analysing a TCP handshake, a DNS query and a TLS session that fails

videos.script: A connection failed, and three people have three theories. {{theories}} This lesson settles arguments like that one by reading the packets. {{wire}} First the TCP handshake, number by number. Three packets open a connection, and the numbers in them count every byte that follows. {{handshake}} Then two ways to fail. A closed port answers at once with a reset. A firewall that drops says nothing, and the client tries again, and again. {{silence}} Then a DNS question and its answer, paired by an id, with a reply code that says the name does not exist. {{dns}} Then TLS. It works once, and fails three times, with an expired certificate, a wrong name and an authority nobody trusts. {{tls}} Two of those failures say why, in clear, on the wire. The third looks exactly like a success. {{alert}} You will learn which is which, ask the server with openssl, and read a failing capture file line by line, until every packet in it is accounted for. {{file}}
